financing.summary: Beazer Homes is no longer a stand-alone borrower: Dream Finders Homes bought it for $33.50 a share in cash (about $878.4M of equity) on 2026-10-20, and Beazer's land and debt now sit inside Dream Finders' land-light, option-heavy model. Before the deal Beazer owned about 40% of its active lots and funded itself with a JPMorgan-led $525M unsecured revolver, $1.0B of senior notes and $100.8M face of junior subordinated notes (net debt to net capital 52.8% at 2026-06-30, up from 39.5% a year earlier). At closing Millrose Properties (managed by Kennedy Lewis) bought about 7,000 Beazer homesites, more than half finished, for about $580M and optioned them back to Dream Finders; that money retired Beazer's 2029 notes and revolver. What is left of Beazer's own capital structure is $650M of 2031 and 2032 notes, almost all being swapped into Dream Finders paper (settlement expected 2026-11-23), and the junior subordinated notes. For a competing land banker, Beazer's remaining owned land and any future land-bank work are now Dream Finders decisions, and Millrose is already in both the land and the capital structure.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving toward more options. Beazer bought lots through option agreements 'with land developers and land bankers' and expected to exercise substantially all of them; it raised the optioned share of active lots from 57.8% (FY2024) to 62.1% (FY2025), then 60.0% at 2026-06-30. No numeric optioned-lot target was stated; its stated FY2027 goals were more than 200 active communities, net debt to net capital in the low 30% range, and book value per share in the mid-$50s. It also sold non-strategic land (more than $100M expected in FY2026, per the CEO) and did a model-home sale-leaseback. Since 2026-10-20 the land is run under Dream Finders' 'asset-light' finished-lot and land-bank option model.

lots.source_title: Beazer Homes fiscal Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)
lots.note: Reported: 24,489 total controlled lots and 23,083 active lots, 60.0% of active lots under option (last reported quarter before the merger; Beazer stopped filing after 2026-10-20). Owned and optioned counts are computed, not reported: optioned = 60.0% x 23,083 = about 13,850; owned = 24,489 - 13,850 = about 10,639 (includes about 1,406 lots held for future development or for sale). pct_optioned is the share of active lots. At 2025-09-30 the 10-K showed 25,660 controlled, 24,758 active, 15,373 optioned (62.1%) and 10,287 owned. Years of supply not stated. At closing about 7,000 of the owned homesites moved to Millrose under options to Dream Finders, so the owned share is now far lower.

land_banking.description: At the Dream Finders closing, certain pre-acquisition Beazer land assets were sold to Millrose and Dream Finders got options to buy the homesites over time on terms like its other land-bank options. Millrose says it funded about $580M (net of option deposits) for about 7,000 homesites, more than half finished, with a weighted-average life of about 2.5 years.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)
land_banking.note: Dream Finders reports $572.1M of proceeds (8-K and 10-Q subsequent-events note); Millrose reports about $580M net of option deposits. The options belong to Dream Finders, not Beazer. Proceeds redeemed Beazer's $350M 2029 notes, repaid its revolver and paid deal costs. Option fee rate not disclosed.

land_banking.description: Commitment letter signed with the merger agreement on 2026-08-06: an $800M land bank facility to fund part of the Beazer purchase price, conditioned on the merger, the preferred investment and a notes or equity offering or bridge draw. Dream Finders' February 2026 proposal carried 'highly confident' letters from financing sources the merger proxy does not name.
land_banking.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Form 8-K (Beazer merger agreement and financing commitments)
land_banking.note: This commitment was ultimately funded through Millrose (Kennedy Lewis is Millrose's external manager) at about $572M to $580M, not the full $800M. Verification 2026-11-19: removed the claim that Kennedy Lewis gave the February 2026 'highly confident' letters; the DEFM14A says only 'certain financing sources'.

land_banking.counterparty: Unnamed land developers and land bankers (Beazer legacy lot options)
land_banking.description: Beazer's own lot option agreements, with deposits and non-refundable pre-acquisition costs of $387.4M and $1,631.3M of remaining purchase price if all options were exercised. Some options are accounted for as product financing (land not owned under option agreements $24.8M; related liability $14.0M), which is new in FY2026.
land_banking.source_title: Beazer 10-Q (2026-06-30), Interests in Lot Option Agreements
land_banking.note: Counterparties are not named in any Beazer filing read; the 10-K only says options are with 'land developers and land bankers' and that land bankers sometimes take title with Beazer obligated to develop the land (typically reimbursed). Lots figure is the computed optioned count from the Q3 FY2026 release. Pre-merger; Dream Finders said it is terminating option deals that miss return thresholds.

debt.lenders_agent: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (administrative agent and issuing lender)
debt.note: principal_usd_m is the amount drawn at 2026-06-30 ($45.8M of letters of credit also outstanding, $139.2M available). Credit agreement dated 2022-10-13; Third Amendment (2026-03-13) raised commitments from $365M to $525M (accordion to $625M, $100M LC sublimit) and extended maturity from 2028-03-15 to 2030-03-13. Repaid in full and terminated at the merger closing on 2026-10-20. Terms per 10-Q borrowings note.

debt.source_title: Dream Finders Homes press release: early participation results of exchange offers for Beazer notes
debt.note: Issued March 2024 (indenture dated 2024-03-15). Change-of-control definition amended by consent so the merger did not trigger a 101% put (supplemental indenture 2026-09-18). Dream Finders' exchange offer into new DFH 7.500% notes due 2031: $248.062M (99.22%) tendered by 2026-11-04; expiry 2026-11-20, settlement expected 2026-11-23, after which about $1.9M would stay as Beazer notes with covenants stripped.

debt.lenders_agent: Regions Bank (trustee); J.P. Morgan Securities (representative of initial purchasers); D.F. King (exchange agent)
debt.source_title: Dream Finders Homes press release: early participation results of exchange offers for Beazer notes
debt.note: Issued 2026-06-23 at par in a 144A offering (indenture dated 2026-06-23) to redeem the 2027 notes. Consent to amend change of control received 2026-09-17. Exchange offer into new DFH 8.000% notes due 2032: $393.125M (98.28%) tendered by 2026-11-04; settlement expected 2026-11-23, leaving about $6.9M as covenant-stripped Beazer notes.

Face $100.8M, carrying value $80.0M. $75.0M restructured in 2010 (floor 4.25%, cap 9.25%, redeemable at 75% of par rising 1.785% a year from 2022); $25.8M on original terms at 3-month SOFR + 2.71%, redeemable at par. Dream Finders said (2026-08-18 8-K) it expected about $80M of these to stay outstanding after the merger; post-closing status not confirmed in a filing read. Trustee not named in the note.
Issued September 2019. Conditional notice given 2026-09-28; redeemed in full on 2026-10-20 at 101.208% plus accrued interest with Millrose land-bank proceeds deposited by Dream Finders.
Remaining $357.3M redeemed at par in the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (notice 2026-06-15) with proceeds of the 2032 notes; $0.7M loss on extinguishment.

ma.description: Dream Finders acquired Beazer in an all-cash merger at $33.50 a share (about $878.4M of equity), and Beazer became a wholly owned subsidiary and delisted. Dream Finders approached privately on 2026-01-16, offered $28.50 (Feb) and $29.00 (Mar), went public on 2026-05-11 with a $25.75 offer the board rejected, raised to $29.25 (June 22) and $32.00 (June 30, public 2026-07-08), and signed at $33.50 on 2026-08-06 (announced 2026-08-07) after rival bidders withdrew. Funded with Series B preferred, Millrose land banking, revolver borrowings and cash. Beazer's advisors were J.P. Morgan and Moelis.
ma.map_impact: Fold Beazer under Dream Finders: it is no longer a separate public builder or borrower. All nine Beazer directors (including Allan Merrill) resigned and were replaced by Dream Finders' directors (Patrick Zalupski, Rick Beckwitt and others); Beazer's officers stayed in their roles at closing (CFO David I. Goldberg signed the closing 8-K), but the combined land and division reporting lines are not published. The JPMorgan revolver and 2029 notes are gone; the 2031 and 2032 notes are becoming Dream Finders notes; about 7,000 Beazer homesites are now Millrose land under option to Dream Finders. Beazer's markets (AZ, CA, NV, TX, IN, MD/DE, TN, VA, FL, GA, NC, SC) are now Dream Finders markets, so land calls go to the Dream Finders team.
ma.note: Offer history from the DEFM14A background section. Dream Finders closing 8-K gives the $878.4M equity consideration.

ma.description: Unnamed strategic bidder contacted 2026-05-11; offered $32.00 cash (June 19) and $33.50 cash (July 9), holding about 3% of Beazer stock; withdrew on 2026-08-02 citing higher financing costs and operational limits in its proposed land bank financing. Party C (strategic, part-stock $32.00 offer on July 2) withdrew 2026-07-29 citing share price, execution risk and land-banking financing; Party A (a real estate developer) proposed contributing its US homebuilding operations for 27% to 40% of the combined company and was not pursued.
ma.map_impact: No change to the map; shows that at least two other builders bidding for Beazer planned to fund it with land-bank capital and walked away over its cost and terms.
ma.source_title: Beazer Homes USA DEFM14A merger proxy statement
ma.note: Bidder identities not disclosed in the proxy.
